reason: The salivary glands have a marked duct connection and a named slot in the digestive tube.
expectation: The glands will fit into the tube with their ducts opening into the mouth.

effect: The salivary glands are fitted; the other named organ slots remain to be filled.
reaction: The duct connection worked as expected.
reason: The pancreas has a named slot and a duct leading to the small intestine.
expectation: The pancreas will fit into the tube with its duct connected to the small intestine.

effect: The pancreas is fitted; the liver and gallbladder remain to be attached.
reaction: The named slot worked as expected.
reason: The liver and gallbladder have a named slot and bile ducts leading toward the intestine.
expectation: The liver and gallbladder will fit into the digestive tube assembly.

effect: The gland, pancreas and liver goal is complete; the meal still needs breaking down.
reaction: The organ fittings worked as expected.
reason: Salivary amylase is shown near starch chains, suggesting it can begin digesting the bread.
expectation: The amylase will begin breaking the starch into smaller carbohydrates.

effect: Salivary amylase shortened the starch chains; further digestion is still needed.
reaction: The initial breakdown was as expected.
reason: The pancreatic and intestinal starch-digesting enzymes are the apparent next step for the shorter chains.
expectation: The enzymes will break the chains into smaller sugars suitable for absorption.

effect: The starch has been broken down into individual glucose molecules; protein and fat remain to be digested.
reaction: The progression from starch chains to glucose was clear.
reason: The protein-digesting enzymes are shown acting on protein chains.
expectation: The enzymes will break the protein into smaller components for absorption.

effect: Protein digestion produced meal amino acids; fat remains to be broken down.
reason: Bile and lipase are shown acting on dietary fat droplets.
expectation: Bile will disperse the fat into smaller droplets, allowing lipase to break it into absorbable components.

effect: Fat digestion produced fatty acids and monoglycerides, completing the remaining goal. The result distinguishes bile’s dispersing role from lipase’s enzymatic action.
reaction: The distinction was useful and matched my expectation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking starch down in two stages made the progression from chains to individual glucose molecules clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the three named organ slots was predictable and repetitive, although it established the digestive system’s layout.

surprise.text: The fat result clarified that bile is not an enzyme: it disperses droplets while lipase breaks fat molecules apart. Monoglycerides were named in the picture plan without further explanation.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless, though the organ fittings relied mainly on matching named slots rather than a meaningful decision.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the digestion products cross the intestinal lining; this chapter ends with them ready for absorption rather than showing that step.
